Each of the following graphics, except one, can be interpretted as a relative probability function. Which is the exception?

```{r}
#| label: fig-hpc-1-u23
#| echo: false
#| layout-ncol: 4
#| fig-cap: "Functions that might be relative probability distributions"
#| fig-subcap:
#| - " "
#| - " "
#| - " "
#| - " " 
r1 <- doodle_fun(~ x, seed = 8382)
r2 <- doodle_fun(~ x, seed = 7482)
r3 <- doodle_fun(~ x, seed = 6382)
r4 <- doodle_fun(~ x, seed = 44482)

slice_plot((r1(6-rainfall) + 8)/3 ~ rainfall, domain(rainfall = 0:6) ) |> gf_labs(x = "Rainfall (in)") |>
  gf_lims(y = c(0, NA)) |>
  gf_theme(theme_minimal(base_size = 18))

slice_plot((abs(r2(rainfall)))/300 ~ rainfall, domain(rainfall = 0:6) ) |> gf_labs(x = "Rainfall (in)") |>
  #gf_lims(y = c(NA, NA)) |>
  gf_theme(theme_minimal(base_size = 18))  

slice_plot(((r4((temperature+30)/25))/3 - 1) ~ temperature, domain(temperature = -20:80) ) |> gf_labs(x = "Temperature (deg)") |>
  gf_lims(y = c(-1, NA)) |>
  gf_theme(theme_minimal(base_size = 18))  

slice_plot((abs(r3((direction+80)/60)))/3 ~ direction, domain(direction = -180:180) ) |> gf_labs(x = "Direction (deg)") |>
  gf_lims(y = c(0, NA)) |>
  gf_theme(theme_minimal(base_size = 18))  
```

`r devoirs::devoirs_set("hpc-1-67s", choices=c("a", "b", "c", "d"), correct = "c")`

:::
